html:
CRYPTO NEWS — August 3, 2026

Markets stayed rangebound on modest selling overnight as macro data dominates the week ahead. Bitcoin dipped 1.40% to $62,445 while altcoins underperformed—ETH -1.80%, SOL -1.30%—on persistent downtrend momentum. Fear sentiment ticked marginally higher to 28 (yesterday: 27), confirming no relief rally yet. Total market cap shed $20B to $2.23T. The real story isn't the price action—it's what didn't happen. The muted reaction to a hawkish Fed hold, a major wallet exploit, and month-end ETF redemptions suggests the market has already discounted substantial negative news. Stablecoin liquidity remains solid at $255.1B, leaving dry powder for moves in either direction. Funding rates stay benign (BTC +0.0048%, ETH -0.0022%), no leverage squeeze imminent.

TODAY'S HIGHLIGHTS

CLARITY Act Racing the Recess Clock — Crypto's Legislative Lifeline
Polymarket odds on 2026 passage fell from above 80% in February to around 35%, with early August now treated as the practical cutoff before Senate recess and election calendar compete for attention. The House passed its version 294-134 on July 17, 2025, and the Senate Banking Committee advanced it 15-9 on May 14, 2026. If the bill dies this window, altcoin risk assets (tokens, DEX/DeFi plays) get orphaned; Bitcoin's driven by ETF flows and macro, so less exposed. Watch Friday's Senate recess opening—if CLARITY slips past this gate, odds collapse further. Traders should hedge token exposure or rotate toward BTC, which remains resilient regardless of legislative outcomes.

Coldcard Firmware Breach — Third Wave of Smaller Wallet Drains
Galaxy Research flagged a third wave of sweeps tied to weak Coldcard-generated keys, with the attacker now targeting smaller balances and changing how funds are collected onchain. This isn't the $70M headline hit from late July—it's the aftershock. Attackers are adapting tactics, switching collection methods to evade tracking. Security fatigue is setting in after weeks of headlines. Takeaway: hardware wallet users need to rotate keys or move to air-gapped setups; exchanges seeing uptick in inbound volume from panicked self-custodians. Expect continued pressure on retail confidence through at least mid-August.

XRP Ledger 3.3.0 Release — Features Once Withdrawn Return After Bug Fixes
The xrpld 3.3.0 release for the XRP Ledger is expected next week, carrying five proposed amendments, including two features previously withdrawn after researchers identified bugs. Timing is flexible; watch validator adoption as the real trigger for price movement. XRP benefited from Polkadot's outperformance (per latest trends) this week, but approval velocity matters more than the upgrade itself. Traders: validation momentum is your signal. Slow uptake = dud; fast rollout = potential squeeze into August consolidation.

WATCH LIST

Friday's US Nonfarm Payrolls report is the week's biggest macro event. A muted rise in US hiring could be the best outcome for risk assets like crypto, as it would ease fears of economic slowdown but wouldn't push the Fed closer to raising rates. Monday's ISM Manufacturing PMI (today) matters less, but watch the prices-paid component for inflation trajectory signals. ETF flows remain tentative—Thursday's $233M net inflow led by BlackRock snapped a four-day outflow streak, but this is still recovery-mode, not conviction. BTC needs to hold above $62,525 (24h low) to avoid weekly support tests; any break triggers $60K liquidity hunt. Altcoins remain structurally weak against BTC; rotation risk persists until ETH reclaims weekly support around $1,800.

See you tomorrow — stay sharp, watch the recess clock, and don't hold extended baggage into Friday's jobs print.
